messages:
alex: quick PSA — noticed a spike in canary exposure this morning, looks like sticky assignments got invalidated after we changed the route hash salt in the rollout meta. users who were pinned to stable suddenly hit canary.
maria: wait wtf. which rollout? show me the config change
alex: rollout id r-2024-11-12, changed `hash_salt` from `v1` -> `v2` to normalize cookie encoding. console saved it and the change propagated to edge without a rebucketing flag.
sam: that explains the telemetry blip — we saw session-affinity churn + canary error rate rise. link to traces? @observability-bot can you paste the query
observability-bot: Datadog query pasted: `avg:service.request.canary_rate{rollout:r-2024-11-12} by {host}.rollup(avg, 60)` -> spike 7x at 09:12 UTC
tia: repro steps? can we reproduce locally against the router shim
alex: repro curl to the router (we use client_id header for hashing):
```
curl -H "X-Client-Id: 7f3e9" -H "Cookie: session=..." https://gateway.internal/api/v1/generate
```
- with `hash_salt=v1` it consistently goes to stable
- with `hash_salt=v2` same client_id -> different bucket
maria: is salt part of the signed cookie? I thought we preserved the bucket if cookie exists
sam: code path: router computes `bucket = hash(client_id + salt) % total_buckets` and we only check cookie if `sticky=true AND cookie.bucket == bucket` — we changed salt so computed bucket != cookie.bucket, so cookie ignored.
tia: so behavior is technically expected but bad UX. Changing salt should either (a) rebucket explicitly, or (b) preserve existing cookie mapping by using cookie.bucket override unless `rebucketize=true`.
alex: agree. console should block salt edits when rollout is active or at least warn strongly.
maria: we need immediate mitigations: 1) rollback the salt change 2) mark rollout frozen 3) emit a backfill job to reassign affected cookies or do a rolling rebucket with low ramp.
sam: rollback done (r-2024-11-12 reverted to v1) — traffic normalized within 5m. but we still need longer term fix.
tia: proposed fix PR: github.com/redwood/routing/pull/589
- add `preserve_cookie_on_salt_change` default true
- console UI: show a modal if hash_salt edit and rollout.active==true with checkbox `Force rebucketize (danger)`
- server: disallow silent salt change when cookies exist (error 422)
alex: also add telemetry alert: if canary_rate deviates >3x baseline within 15m after rollout meta change -> page oncall
observability-bot: alert draft: `route.hash_salt_change_causes_affinity_churn` -> fire on `sum:router.affinity.invalidate{env:prod} by {rollout} > 0.02 * sum:router.requests{env:prod} by {rollout}`
maria: one more thing — migration tooling: a job that reads cookie store and issues `Set-Cookie` to rewrite bucket according to new salt for opted-in customers. need to get privacy/legal signoff.
sam: will sketch the migration as a bounded-rate job + dry-run mode. also add integration test for sticky continuity on salt changes.
tia: filing infra tasks:
- ENG-1304 console guard
- ENG-1305 router server validation
- ENG-1306 telemetry alert + dashboard card
- ENG-1307 migration job (dry-run)
alex: thanks. can someone take ENG-1304 and ENG-1305? this is priority P1 for rollouts UX.
maria: taking ENG-1304, will mock modal copy and add telemetry link
sam: taking ENG-1305, will add validation and unit tests
tia: I'll own ENG-1306 and ENG-1307 — will coordinate with privacy and schedules
alex: perfect. we'll post a short blameless RCA to #postmortems after we finish the fixes.
maria: small nit for console: add a diff view for rollout meta changes — saves folks from accidental salt edits
alex: agreed. thanks all :thumbsup:
